title: Cannabis Mineral Nutrition, Interactions and Diagnostic Limits
summary: Mineral nutrition is an interacting system shaped by element supply, root-zone conditions, developmental stage and genotype; visual symptoms or one nutrient value rarely establish a complete diagnosis.

sections.title: Nutrients interact rather than act independently
sections.body: Controlled cannabis nutrition research has documented interactions among nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium and changes in tissue composition as formulations change. This means a response attributed to one element may partly reflect altered uptake or balance of other nutrients.

sections.title: More nutrient is not automatically more performance
sections.body: Recent cannabis root-zone research found that increasing phosphorus and overall nutrient concentration above adequate treatment levels could increase accumulation without improving yield or cannabinoid outcomes under the studied conditions, illustrating diminishing return and accumulation risk.

sections.title: Diagnosis needs multiple evidence streams
sections.body: Visual deficiency symptoms can overlap with irrigation, root damage, pH, salinity or disease, and research shows symptom onset does not always map simply onto foliar concentration. Strong diagnosis integrates spatial pattern, tissue sampling, root-zone data and environmental history.
